body:
(1) Most serious: lines 183-184 (timeout) combined with state() lines 108-114. The waiter measures the timeout from its own last message's mtime (line 178) and, on expiry, unilaterally writes an abort file. From then on every command by anyone returns "closed", so the peer's legitimate late reply is rejected and its work is lost. There is no heartbeat, so a slow-but-alive peer is indistinguishable from a dead one. Related: for n==0 (line 178) the clock starts at `started`, so the docstring's claim that it "survives re-runs" is false; each re-run of recv resets it, and a primary that never sends can wait forever.

(2) Docstring unclear points: whether "waiting" counts against the timeout; what max_wait_minutes applies to when the secondary has not seen message 0 yet; whether the secondary's own selftest failure should be reported with --end "REFUSED:" before the first recv, when it is not its turn to send (send would error "not your turn", line 153).
